findings.summary: net_offsetting_orders() builds the NET order from only a subset of fields. It drops hard_no_chase_ceiling_vnd, ceiling_rule/anchor/tau, hard_sell_floor_vnd and cash_only from the lead leg, so these hard guards disappear for any ticker that gets netted.
findings.evidence: plan.py:415-426 constructs PlannedOrder(id=..., ticker, side, qty, ref_price=lead.ref_price, book, play_type, priority, urgency, note, dcf_check, dcf_override_reason, dd_check, dd_override_reason). It does not copy hard_no_chase_ceiling_vnd, hard_sell_floor_vnd or cash_only. Pipeline order in bot_execute.py: load_plan (plan.py:256-265 sets hard_no_chase_ceiling_vnd at the load boundary) -> ... -> bot_execute.py:591 net_offsetting_orders. Nothing restores the ceiling afterwards: grep for hard_no_chase_ceiling_vnd/cash_only in bot_execute.py returns nothing, and executor.py:838/852/1041 reads the field from the order via getattr(...). dd_flag_order_gate_selfcheck.py:260-266 (NET-C) shows a real NET order with lead book=DISCRETIONARY_SPECIAL (the book that carries cash_only + hard ceiling, case TV1/UPCOM).
findings.suggested_fix: In net_order, copy from lead (only when side matches): hard_no_chase_ceiling_vnd + the 4 ceiling_* fields for buy, hard_sell_floor_vnd for sell, cash_only. For buy, take min() of the ceilings across all buy legs and max() of the floors across sell legs (the tighter bound). Add a selfcheck: BUY with ceiling + smaller SELL on the same ticker => the NET BUY keeps the ceiling.

findings.summary: approval_block_reason() treats any non-empty approved_by string as approved, except none/null/nil/nan. A plan with requires_user_approval=true and approved_by='auto'/'pending'/'false'/'DollarBill' passes the approval gate and runs live, even though the file already defines APPROVAL_PLACEHOLDERS listing exactly these strings.
findings.evidence: plan.py:2240-2247: if approved.lower() in ('none','null','nil','nan'): approved = '' / if approved: return None. Meanwhile plan.py:1143-1145 APPROVAL_PLACEHOLDERS = ('', 'none', ..., 'false', '0', 'pending', 'tbd', 'auto', 'agent', 'bot', 'system', 'mike', 'dollarbill', ...) is used only by margin_day_approval (plan.py:1340). Real precedent: grep data/trade_plans/*.json finds 6 plans (SpaceX 2026-07-07..07-13) where the generator wrote approved_by='auto' (that time with requires_user_approval=False, so the gate was not exercised).
findings.suggested_fix: In approval_block_reason, replace the 4-string tuple with APPROVAL_PLACEHOLDERS (approved.lower() in APPROVAL_PLACEHOLDERS => treat as unapproved). Add a selfcheck case: requires_user_approval=true + approved_by='auto'/'pending' => blocked.

findings.summary: --accept-gdkhq-by defaults to 'user'. Running --accept-gdkhq-shadow (which turns on live D1-D3 GDKHQ) without the flag writes accepted_by='user' into the acceptance state, even when an agent ran it: a fabricated 'user approved' record on the money path.
findings.evidence: bot_execute.py:447: ap.add_argument('--accept-gdkhq-by', default='user', ...); :508 accept_gdkhq_shadow(args.accept_gdkhq_shadow, args.accept_gdkhq_by, ...); trading_bot/gdkhq_rollout.py:205 writes 'accepted_by': str(accepted_by). §20: mark 'user' only when the user actually confirmed in real time.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the default (required=True when --accept-gdkhq-shadow is used), or reject 'user'/empty/APPROVAL_PLACEHOLDERS and require a specific name + approval reference.

findings.summary: terminal_growth() hardcodes cpi_monthly_df(end='2026-12-01'). From 2027-01 on, the 5-year CPI window silently loses the newest months: the mean is taken over a series cut off at 12/2026, and cpi_coverage() does not warn because it only checks up to that same hardcoded end.
findings.evidence: dcf_valuation.py:400-404: _CPI_DF = _cpi.cpi_monthly_df(end='2026-12-01'); w = cpi[(cpi.time <= a) & (cpi.time > a - 365*years)]. cpi_vn.py:361 cpi_coverage(end) only reports the gap up to end. Example: asof=2027-04-15 -> the window is missing 2027-01..04, g_T/g_terminal_frac_real are computed on the old window and nothing prints. Today is 2026-11-08, so this kicks in in under 2 months. (Under domestic_v2, g = min(cpi+gdp, 5.5%), so the FV impact is often capped, but g_terminal_frac_real and the legacy frame are affected directly.)
findings.suggested_fix: Pass end = month start of asof (or today ICT), and key the cache by end, so cpi_coverage() warns correctly when a month has no real source.

findings.summary: Section D asserts on the current production config instead of an invariant. It turns red when the user changes an unrelated flag or turns off the paper trial, even though the dc_book code is correct.
findings.evidence: dc_book_waterfall_selfcheck.py:230-231 ok('D1 chase_cap_vol_scale is LIVE (default True since 2026-08-04)', DEFAULTS.get('chase_cap_vol_scale_enabled') is True) is an executor flag unrelated to this module. :233-234 profiles = load_accounts(load_config()); ok('D2 main resolves flag ON', profiles['main']['cfg'].get('dc_book_waterfall_enabled') is True) reads the real trading_bot_accounts.json. :408 ok('E5 v1 NAV series archived', os.path.exists(data/dc_book_waterfall_paper_nav_v1.csv)) depends on a production artifact. (§23 corollary 1)
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the chase_cap_vol_scale assert. Replace D2/E5 with an invariant: no live account (mode=live) has the flag ON. The 'main ON' check belongs in ops_health, not the selfcheck.

findings.summary: The 'double-confirm' rule (sector_lens status=BUY AND 8L rating ≤2) is copied by hand in at least 3 files, which will drift when the threshold changes in one place.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'int(rt) <= 2': converge_report.py:61 (_live_double_confirm), dc_book_waterfall_paper.py:402 (load_double_confirm, docstring :393 'Identical selection to converge_report._live_double_confirm'), newdeals_daily_report.py:99. All three bodies are the same: slm.compute_status() -> df[df.status=='BUY'] -> ratings.get(t) <= 2 -> buy_mode or 'ACCUMULATE'.
findings.suggested_fix: Move it into one function (e.g. sector_lens_monitor.double_confirm_set()) and have all 3 consumers call it. Keep each caller's fail mode as is ({} vs None).

findings.summary: When a held name has no close on the advance day (suspended or missing from the cache), r_i is set to 0, and new_close drops that name. From then on c0 is permanently None, so the return between the last known close and the resumption price is never booked into the paper NAV.
findings.evidence: dc_book_waterfall_paper.py:634-635: c0, c1 = prev_close.get(t), closes.get(t); r_i = (c1/c0 - 1.0) if (c0 and c1) else 0.0. :679 new_close = {t: closes[t] for t in target_w if t in closes}, so a name with no close today drops out of last_close while its weight stays in target_w (drifted). On resumption day c0 = None, so r_i = 0 again and the gap (e.g. -20% during the halt) is lost permanently, overstating cum_pnl_pct.
findings.suggested_fix: Carry forward the old close for names with no price today: new_close = {t: closes.get(t, prev_close.get(t)) ...} and log/flag the day's row as having a missing price (no silent 0).

findings.summary: The freshness-gate test asserts the gap is exactly the 4 months 2026-09..12. That value depends on NSO_CPI_YOY_REAL currently ending at 2026-06 and TE being off. Doing the fix the warning itself recommends (refresh NSO_CPI_YOY_REAL from GSO) turns the selfcheck red even though the code is correct.
findings.evidence: cpi_vn_tier15_selfcheck.py:168-171: ok([str(d.date()) for d in gap2] == ['2026-09-01','2026-10-01','2026-11-01','2026-12-01'], ...). cpi_vn.py:305 warning: 'FIX = refresh NSO_CPI_YOY_REAL from the GSO monthly release'. Also test_dcf :266/:286 requires all 7 named tickers (CSV, DGC, DRI, NCT, SAB, TV1, VNM) to price on live data (bq_cache) via ok(len(priced) == 7).
findings.suggested_fix: Assert on the relation instead: gap2 == the months from max(real_last, fp_last)+1 to 2026-12 (computed from the module's own tier data); in test_dcf require len(priced) >= 3.

findings.summary: latest_price_session(asof) only falls back to 2*.parquet when the year file errors on read. If the year file exists but has no row ≤asof for the ticker (asof = 1/1 holiday, or a ticker halted early in January), it returns (None, None) and dcf_check reports NOT_COMPUTED 'no_price', even though the previous year has a price.
findings.evidence: dcf_valuation.py:1030-1040: yr = str(year(asof)); try: read_parquet('.../ticker/{yr}.parquet') WHERE ticker=... AND time <= asof LIMIT 1 / except: read '2*.parquet'; if len(df) == 0: return None, None. By contrast price_session_for (:913-923) already reads both {a.year-1} and {a.year}.
findings.suggested_fix: Read both the {yr-1} and {yr} files (like price_session_for), or fall back to 2*.parquet when df is empty, not only on exception.

findings.summary: TradePlan.save() stamps created_at with a bare datetime.now(), which depends on the host TZ (debt already recorded in tz_anchor_baseline: trading_bot/plan.py=1).
findings.evidence: plan.py:122: d['created_at'] = d['created_at'] or dt.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec='seconds'). mike/kb/tz_anchor_baseline.json files['trading_bot/plan.py'] = 1. executor.py:345 only compares created_at for equality, so trading logic is unaffected, but the timestamp is wrong under cron env -u TZ.
findings.suggested_fix: Use dt.datetime.now(ZoneInfo('Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh')) and lower the baseline with --update-baseline.

findings.summary: The 'new version still print-only' assertion is a tautology. The condition `needle not in new or '_notify_failopen' in new` is always true once line 83 has confirmed _notify_failopen is in new, so the check can never fail.
findings.evidence: failopen_telegram_refresh_selfcheck.py:83 ok(f'_notify_failopen(p["label"], "{gate}"' in new, ...) runs before :93 ok(needle not in new or '_notify_failopen' in new, f'#1 bản MỚI vẫn còn print-only cho {needle!r}'). The second operand is guaranteed True, so an old print-only line left in bot_execute.py would not be caught.
findings.suggested_fix: Change it to ok(needle not in new, ...) (the new version must not keep the old print line).
